title: Reproducing Raider and Flitsch 1978: width and composition of the silicon-to-oxide transition region

sample.paper: “chemically cleaned and etched 1-2 ohm-cm Si substrates that had either (100) or (111) surface orientations and possessed either p- or n-type dopant”
sample.ours: FAMILY: Si_Planar; ORIENTATION: Si100 or Si111

sample.paper: p- or n-type, 1-2 Ω·cm; dopant species not stated; substrate δ reference holds for dopant < 10^18 cm⁻³
sample.ours: DOPING: n_or_p_1_to_2_ohm_cm (recorded; no program reads it)
sample.note: Which films were n and which p is not stated; the authors find no dependence.
The vocabulary's cleans do not include an unnamed chemical clean; not_stated is the nearest.

sample.paper: 200 nm dry oxide at 1050 °C, removed in HF
sample.ours: EVENT SacrificialOxide and EVENT Strip; the simulated wafer starts bare
sample.note: The strip leaves an HF-etched surface; STARTING_OXIDE_NM is not set because the thin-oxide program's fitted start stands in for its first growth.

sample.paper: carbon 0.2-0.3 nm on oxide, 0.5-0.6 nm on unoxidized Si
sample.note: No field for an adsorbed layer.

sample.paper: < 3.0 nm; < 1.3 nm at 23 °C; about 1.1 nm minimum at 850 °C; < 1.8 nm after boiling water (from escape depth)

history.item: Chemically cleaned and etched (recipe not stated)
history.paper: “grown on chemically cleaned and etched 1-2 ohm-cm Si substrates”
history.note: The cleaning chemistry is not given.

history.paper: “Cleaned Si wafers were initially oxidized at 1050°C in dry O2 to form oxide films 200 nm thick.”
history.note: Simulating it would leave 200 nm of oxide on the wafer: the language has no statement that removes oxide, so the strip that follows could not undo it. Its time is not stated (about 3 h for 200 nm at 1050 °C by the 1965 law).

history.item: Oxide removed in HF, rinsed in deionized water, dried
history.paper: “The oxide films were then removed by etching in HF. The wafers were subsequently rinsed in deionized water, dried, and reoxidized.”
history.ours: EVENT Strip KIND etch; the simulated wafer starts bare
history.note: HF concentration and etch time not stated.
Room-temperature regrowth in air before reoxidation is not known; for the room-temperature samples it is the oxidation itself.

history.paper: “oxidations in air and in water, using n- and p-type substrates with primarily (100), but also (111), substrate surface orientations. Film thicknesses were < 1.3 nm.”; 23 °C from the legend of Figure 5
history.ours: RUN AirExposure DURATION 3600 TEMP 23->23 AMBIENT mix:O2=0.21,N2=0.79
history.note: Duration not stated (the paper refers to its ref. 18). One hour is ours; air is written as 21% oxygen in nitrogen, its humidity is not stated. Oxidation in water at room temperature, the other room-temperature oxidant, cannot be written: the language has no liquid ambient.

history.ours: the history ends when the oxidation ends

history.item: Ellipsometry at 546.1 nm, n = 1.46 assumed, measured rapidly
history.paper: “Film thicknesses of films prepared at elevated temperatures were rapidly measured to minimize the buildup of surface contamination.”
history.note: “In the oxide thickness range under consideration, n cannot be determined from ellipsometric measurements.”

history.item: XPS, Mg Kα, AEI ES-100: Si(2p) shift δ, intensity ratio R, linewidths, O(1s)/Si(2p)
history.paper: “An AEI ES-100 electrostatic analyzer was used to obtain photoelectron spectra. Samples were excited with Mg Kα (1253.6 eV) radiation.”
history.ours: no observable: the language has no XPS observation model
history.note: Time in air before XPS not stated. Some O(1s) samples were heated in the XPS vacuum to 400 °C (PDF p. 8).

history.ours: not written: the language has no liquid ambient

history.paper: “boiling aqueous solutions [H2O, HNO3, H2O2(30 percent)] for one hour”
history.ours: only boiling water, as steam at 100 °C
history.note: Nitric acid and peroxide oxidize silicon chemically; no ambient in the language names them.

history.paper: “Many of the data shown in Fig. 10 were selected after oxidation or annealing within the XPS vacuum system at temperatures to 400°C”
history.note: Affects the O(1s)/Si(2p) data only, which are not compared here.

history.ours: one annealed case and one unannealed case
